title: Kipu Quantum Launches Rimay Quantum Feature Extraction in IBM Quantum Functions Catalog - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Kipu Quantum released its Rimay quantum feature-extraction service in the IBM Quantum Functions Catalog as a drop-in preprocessing layer for classical ML, citing modest classifier uplift and a 22-to-2-minute QPU runtime cut moving from Heron r3 to Nighthawk r2. It extends Kipu from optimization into ML and cites a Fortune 100 deployment.

insights.claim: Kipu Quantum made its Rimay quantum feature extraction service available in the IBM Quantum Functions Catalog, giving IBM Quantum Flex, Premium and On-Prem Plan users API access to quantum-enhanced machine learning.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM's catalog is becoming a marketplace for third-party quantum software, a distribution channel for startups.
insights.locator: Quantum software developer Kipu Quantum has made

insights.claim: Rimay follows Kipu's earlier Iskay Quantum Optimizer catalog release, expanding the company's commercial footprint on IBM hardware from combinatorial optimization into tabular and multimodal feature engineering.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Product-line breadth suggests Kipu is building a platform rather than a single-use tool.
insights.locator: Quantum software developer Kipu Quantum has made

insights.claim: Kipu Quantum said Rimay was recently deployed with a Fortune 100 enterprise on an IBM Quantum Nighthawk processor to improve customer-intent prediction models on tabular datasets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An unnamed blue-chip customer hints at real enterprise pilots, though details are undisclosed.
insights.locator: Kipu Quantum noted that Rimay was recently deployed

insights.claim: On a 48-qubit German credit dataset job (1,000 samples, 5,000 shots), Rimay's QPU usage fell from 22 minutes on IBM Heron r3 (ibm_boston) to 2 minutes on Nighthawk r2 (ibm_phoenix).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An ~11x QPU-time reduction across hardware generations directly lowers per-job cost for cloud quantum users.

insights.claim: A hybrid Random Forest using both classical and Rimay quantum features raised recall from 0.921 to 0.957 and AUC from 0.781 to 0.798 over classical baselines.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The uplift is real but modest; investors should treat quantum ML advantage claims as incremental, not transformative.

insights.claim: Rimay supports up to 156 features (one qubit per feature) and 15,000 samples per job, with Small, Medium and Large compute tiers up to 10 million shots.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Capacity limits define which enterprise datasets are in scope today.

insights.claim: Rimay is designed as a drop-in preprocessing layer between train-test splitting and classical model training, returning an enriched CSV matrix usable in scikit-learn, XGBoost, CatBoost or LightGBM rather than replacing existing models.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Low-friction integration into existing data science stacks lowers adoption barriers for quantum ML.
insights.quote: Rather than replacing established machine learning models, Rimay operates as a drop-in preprocessing layer
insights.locator: Rather than replacing established machine learning models

insights.claim: Rimay maps normalized numerical features to individual qubits, encodes pairwise mutual information into Hamiltonian coupling terms, and runs digitized counterdiabatic circuits to extract single-body expectations and two-body qubit correlations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Explains the mechanism behind the claimed feature enrichment.
insights.locator: Rather than replacing established machine learning models

insights.claim: Rimay stores the trained Hamiltonian topology under a persistent mapping_id so new data can be transformed without re-fitting, and can be paired with Kipu's offline classical surrogate to remove quantum hardware dependence during high-volume inference.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A classical surrogate for inference implies quantum hardware may be needed mainly at training time, which caps recurring QPU revenue per customer.
insights.quote: eliminate quantum hardware dependencies during high-volume inference
